answer: Require every agent to lock a small refundable stake before it can transact, recorded on a public reputation ledger. A sybil spawning a thousand identities must fund each one, so the attack's cost scales linearly with its size while honest agents recover their stake after clean history. Older accounts carry a relic of verified work new identities cannot fake, so the economy weighs long-lived reputations like a jetty anchoring ships against a tide, while fresh accounts open slowly like a lotus, earning full rate limits only after proven participation.
